A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from EvE to RefinedFields. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including content moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic and Phototourism reconstruction results, prior and fine-tuning ablations, and a reduced-training-data Lego experiment.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds visual comparisons of learned feature planes in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains alternating K-Planes fitting and refinement through the Stable Diffusion U-Net, LoRA and decoder, with matching training objectives. V2's explicit last-timestep inference and fixed-noise descriptions clarify the existing procedure rather than establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use eight NeRF Synthetic scenes, Brandenburg Gate, Sacré Coeur and Trevi Fountain from Phototourism, and the half-training-set Lego scenario. The synthetic benchmark moves to Appendix D; the new feature inspection also uses Lego.

E2.justification: Corresponding Phototourism and synthetic tables retain their comparator sets, including NeRF-W, Ha-NeRF, CR-NeRF, K-Planes, TensoRF, Plenoxels and INGP where previously evaluated. EvE-F and EvE-P become RefinedFields-noFinetuning and RefinedFields-noPrior. Newly cited methods are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark splits, metrics, model dimensions and training budgets remain unchanged. Appendix C adds a qualitative evaluation procedure: randomly selected feature channels from each orthogonal plane are compared at intermediate and final optimization stages and against final K-Planes-SS representations.

E4.justification: V2 adds a targeted feature-plane analysis in Appendix C and Figures 5–7, examining resemblance to scene projections and the effect of refinement on feature detail. The existing prior ablation, LoRA ablation and restricted-data Lego analysis remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. Random selection of displayed feature channels in v2 does not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The benchmark scores and training times are identical in corresponding tables. V2 adds qualitative feature-plane findings but omits v1 Section 4.5's full-data Lego MSE values, 3.37e-4 for K-Planes and 2.6e-4 for EvE. The half-data MSE values remain in v2 Figure 3.

T1.justification: V2 Equation (5) expresses the existing least-squares refinement objective as projection onto attainable network outputs. This reformulates the optimization already specified in v1 Equation (8); the remaining mathematical objectives are equivalent, and neither version supplies new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The novelty claim broadens from first leveraging generative priors to first leveraging pre-trained networks for in-the-wild scene modeling. V2 also drops v1's explicit claim of easy generative-model interchangeability and future-proofing. The central alternating-refinement and performance claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains refinement through projection onto network-attainable representations and links image-like, orthogonal feature structure to the choice of Stable Diffusion. Its new Impact Statement discusses privacy risks from tourist photographs and inherited diffusion-model biases. The training-time limitation is retained and more explicitly compared with K-Planes.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies inference at the diffusion model's last timestep and explicitly states that Gaussian input noise is fixed during refinement. Software versions, hardware and listed hyperparameters remain unchanged. The project-page address changes, while both versions still promise a future open-source code release.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion or citations for PixelNeRF, DietNeRF, NeRDi, MVDream and diffusion privacy/bias research, while removing the ShapeNet and Imagen references. It also identifies CR-NeRF as concurrent work. These extend the prior-based positioning without replacing its central relationship to earlier research.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the method throughout, v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, proposal and prior-related discussion, and expands the mechanism explanation. It reorganizes the experimental narrative, moves synthetic benchmark reporting into the appendix, converts the discussion into training-time analysis, and restructures the appendices.

P2.justification: V2 adds three substantial feature-plane figure grids, redesigns the related-work table with a referenced appendix counterpart, and redistributes existing figures and tables. The synthetic results and hyperparameters share an appendix page, and captions, typography and page layout change throughout. All original embedded images are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through explicit last-timestep and fixed-noise documentation, and Appendix C provides useful visual evidence for its mechanism explanation. The benchmark evidence remains unchanged. These gains outweigh the limited loss of the full-data Lego MSE comparison, supporting a modest overall improvement.
